headline: Last session: Sensex rose 300 points, though markets logged a seventh straight weekly decline.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 28 September.

why: Rising global yields and oil prices pressured the indices
Sustained foreign fund outflows contributed to a seven-week slide
Recovery in auto and consumer durable sectors provided support in the final session
A sharp 1,200-point crash earlier in the week was driven by weak global cues
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty 50 recorded their seventh consecutive weekly decline
On the last trading day, Sensex ended over 300 points higher
The market hit a three-month low during the week following a major sell-off
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated India has not missed the AI bus
summary: Indian indices concluded their seventh straight week of losses despite a 300-point recovery in the Sensex during Friday's session. The market faced significant headwinds from rising oil prices, elevated global yields, and consistent selling by foreign investors. Although the auto and consumer durable sectors showed resilience, the broader sentiment remains cautious after the indices touched three-month lows.
